tool_definitions.name: depth_query
tool_definitions.description: Query saved permitted RGB-D numerically when enabled. request.kind selects measured depth/region geometry, bounded grasp/place hypotheses, before/after comparison or episode-local target-handle management. Returns small numerical summaries with quality/uncertainty, target/candidate IDs and source observations, not raw point clouds. Candidate IDs require the same current observation. Feed chosen poses to robot_action; a fitted visible surface does not establish full-object shape, contact, retention or task success. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"fixed","kind":"depth_points","observation_id":"obs_1","pixels":[[320,240]]}}

tool_definitions.name: geometry_query
tool_definitions.description: Compute calibrated RGB/proprioception geometry from saved permitted observations. request.kind selects camera/FK, rays, triangulation, pixel_plane intersections with a caller-assumed plane, point/path projection, tracking, batch (1..32 geometry queries in one call via queries=[...]) or explicitly reconstructed-scene queries. Prefer triangulate across two calibrated views (such as head and wrist) when a target feature is visible and matchable in both views, since it measures 3D position without assuming a plane height. Use pixel_plane on demand when a target or destination lies on a known support/table/container plane or when single-view occlusion/weak texture prevents reliable two-view matching: it returns a conditional point (not measured depth), d_point_d_normal_offset_m and cross_camera_projections in other calibrated views, plus optional plane_origin_alt_m sensitivity (assumption_delta_m) and optional target_camera_id overlay image; verify the plane hypothesis via cross_camera_projections or target_camera_id before choosing robot_action targets. Returns numerical value, source/quality/degeneracy evidence and projection images when applicable. build_scene returns a proposed patch without applying it or creating a saved scene_version; scene queries require an existing saved version. No native object truth, movement or physics rollout. Projection images are returned as independent image items. Depth kinds use the depth_query contract only when RGB-D is enabled. In this run pixel_plane also accepts plane_source:'vggt', which replaces your plane height with an image-based estimate of the object's centre height at that pixel (alternate: its top); check value.plane_estimate.quality. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"camera_id":"fixed","kind":"pixel_ray","observation_id":"obs_1","pixel":[320,240]}}

tool_definitions.name: history_annotate_action
tool_definitions.description: Append your textual judgment to an existing action and return the saved annotation. Does not alter measured state, receipts or execution status. Keep interpretations and uncertainty separate from physical evidence. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"action_id":"act_1","note":"The object is released; landing remains uncertain behind the rim."}

examples.note: The object is released; landing remains uncertain behind the rim.

tool_definitions.name: history_list_actions
tool_definitions.description: Read action history in recorded request order without execution or new observation. Optional anchor ('events', 'failures', 'gripper_commands', 'all') returns a top-level episode overview and compact observation-action-receipt-observation blocks with typed execution/partial/failure evidence, observation IDs, measured_delta across execution_start to result, gripper command locations and explicit evidence gaps. The latest action receipt is already returned inline by robot_action; use anchor='failures', 'gripper_commands' or 'events' on demand during multi-step recovery or long-horizon tasks when you need to compare earlier attempts, check cumulative measured_delta, or audit prior gripper commands before planning the next adjustment. Use robot_action_status detail='full' for an action's full stored request/receipt and history_read_trace for saved traces. Without anchor, summary returns a paged status index with total/next_start; full returns the original complete list and cannot be combined with anchor/start/limit. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"anchor":"events","limit":5,"start":0} ; {"limit":25,"start":0}

tool_definitions.name: history_read_trace
tool_definitions.description: Read a saved action's planned, dispatched, measured or before-state JSON evidence without execution. summary preserves exact values and pages long sequences, reporting JSON Pointer paths and next_start. full returns original evidence and cannot be combined with path/start/limit. Missing trace returns unavailable; planned commands are not measurements. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"action_id":"act_1","detail":"summary","kind":"actual_trace","limit":25,"path":"/samples","start":0}

tool_definitions.name: history_view_observation
tool_definitions.description: Read saved permitted RGB and capture-time measured state/calibration without capturing a new frame. Returns images, observation_is_current and separately identified current budget. Optional image_delivery ('none', 'focus_roi', 'head_only', 'all') controls image transport; optional focus_3d projects a 3D target_m (so101_base m) or object_id sphere to 1:1 native-sensor crops with crop_xywh_px=[crop_x,crop_y,w,h], projected_center_uv_px and full_uv = [crop_x + local_u, crop_y + local_v]. Manual camera_id selects one view and roi/scale crop or enlarge it while recording the pixel transform (mutually exclusive with focus_3d). Historical frames remain historical; full repeats saved geometry metadata. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"camera_id":"fixed","observation_id":"obs_1","roi":[100,100,80,60],"scale":2} ; {"focus_3d":{"cameras":["fixed","wrist"],"target_m":[0.22,0.0,0.06]},"observation_id":"obs_1"}

tool_definitions.name: operation_memory
tool_definitions.description: Query or record useful operation experience for any action, including approach, grasp, transport, placement and retreat. Choose scope='task' for this task or 'shared' for cross-task lessons; queries keep the scopes separate. query requires kind and scope; optional operation is an exact case-insensitive category (up to 80 characters), query is search words (up to 200 characters), and limit is an integer 1..30, default 5. record requires kind, scope, operation (up to 80 characters), summary (up to 800 characters), action_ids and observation_ids. Optional conditions is up to 400 characters and is required for shared records; supplied text must be nonblank. Record only a short summary, applicable conditions, operation and actual action/observation IDs. Each ID list requires 1..12 unique recorded IDs, each at most 200 characters; observation_ids must include each action's recorded result observation (input observation only when no result exists). Use only observations linked to those actions; execution facts are read from history. Completed commands do not prove object success. Before reusing shared lessons, inspect current observations and re-localize; never reuse source scene coordinates blindly. request={kind:'help'} shows the fields. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"request":{"kind":"help"}}

tool_definitions.name: pose_plan
tool_definitions.description: Read-only pose planning from the object table; no motion, no action edits. kind='targets': record whether final object orientation matters for this task and, if so, each moved object's absolute end rotation (long-axis yaw in world degrees, upright or lying, optional pitch/roll); returns attention_text to keep in task_plan attention. kind='grasp': for one object-table row (object id from the table attached to the latest observation, or copied row values) returns its geometry facts (centre, top, bottom, length, width, yaw, tilt), angles_deg with the jaws closing across the long axis (object yaw +/- 90 deg, the candidate nearer the arm's measured yaw), the width check against the 88 mm maximum opening, the pad height reference (centre z) and a one-line self_prompt; the grasp point itself is your choice (an optional grasp_point_m + reason is placed relative to the footprint). kind='place': converts an object end yaw into the gripper yaw at release. All values derive from VGGT estimates (not measurements); check them against current RGB. Angles use robot_action's angles_deg=[pitch,roll,yaw] convention: [0,0,0] is top-down with the jaws closing along world x; yaw rotates that line about world +z.

tool_definitions.name: program_run
tool_definitions.description: Start bounded Python or resume a job paused for your action review. Start supplies source/source_ref; resume supplies job_id, review_id and approve/reject, without replacing the invocation. Defaults: 180 seconds work time, 1 GiB memory, numerical libraries use one thread; own helper-model/review waits do not consume work time. New robot actions pause for actor review unless allow_direct_actions=true at start. Approve via this tool, never separately execute the program's cached plan. Returns job/process status, broker action summary, authored stdout/stderr, pending review and final observation. Process exit 0 or tool success does not prove robot/task success. In source use from ni_rua_client import NiRuaClient, ActionIncompleteError; client.action(..., require_completed=True) raises ActionIncompleteError (with .receipt and .response) whenever receipt.status != 'completed' so loops stop immediately on failure or pause; client.call(name,args) returns success/kind/data and display contentItems. For kind='action', read r['data']['receipt'] (one receipt level); for kind='plan', data is the preview or planning rejection. Missing/untyped data remains unknown; do not infer execution from display text. client.artifact(ref) returns permitted bytes; print the fields needed for the next decision (IDs, status/reason, measured errors and selected diagnostics), retaining full artifact references for deeper reads. Leave at least 5 seconds between each inner action timeout and remaining program time; inspect partial/unknown execution and missing observations before any further action. Tool calls are not capped; program tools cannot be called recursively from a program. In summary, stdout and stderr retain all available saved log text; no head/tail byte cap removes middle diagnostics. *_truncated and *_excerpt.source_complete report incomplete sources or media omission. Inline image data URLs are replaced by explicit placeholders in summary only; the excerpt reports original byte size, removed-media ranges, and whether its ranges address presentation text. Repeated unchanged log text over 256 bytes from the same job in this model context is omitted with *_delivery.status='unchanged'; process/action/review status is still returned. Read program_status with the returned job_id and detail='full' to repeat logs or include inline media. full always reads all available saved log text, including on repeated calls; displayed references may use aliases. Read stdout_ref/stderr_ref with client.artifact for exact saved bytes. program_run/program_status automatically forward images from read-only or preview program tools (including history views and geometry overlays), alongside pending-review/final-observation images. Images are separate inputImage items; do not print base64 to expose them. Forwarding preserves the returned imageUrl, ROI and labels without re-encoding. visual_feedback links supplementary images to their source tool/call, arguments and saved reply_ref; historical images remain historical. Repeated unchanged supplementary images in the same model context may be omitted in summary with previous_tool_call_id and a full-result lookup; full or a reset model context delivers them again. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"operation":"start","source":"from ni_rua_client import NiRuaClient\nprint(NiRuaClient().call('robot_observe', {})['data']['observation_id'])"} ; {"decision":"approve","job_id":"job_1","operation":"resume","review_id":"review_1"}

tool_definitions.name: program_status
tool_definitions.description: Read an existing Python job without starting or resuming it. Returns process status, broker action facts, review state and program-authored stdout/stderr. Once the process is terminal, repeated summary reads add no process progress; use full when saved detail or supplementary images are needed. awaiting_review requires program_run resume rather than polling for completion. Authored output and process success are not verified robot/task outcomes. Output logging, stdout/stderr truncation, unchanged-log omission, artifact references and visual_feedback image forwarding follow the same rules as program_run. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"detail":"full","job_id":"job_1"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_action
tool_definitions.description: Unified bounded robot action. Default mode=preview plans the COMPLETE stage batch without moving the robot, returns plan_id, cost, the per-stage IK joint targets with their residuals and robot-geometry evidence. Review it, then call this SAME tool with mode=execute and plan_id to run those cached joint targets: IK is not re-solved, the joint path is re-interpolated from the joints measured at execution (refused if the arm drifted from the preview start) and bounded arrival corrections are reported. No silent replanning. mode=execute_if_clean (or auto_execute_if_clean=true) plans the complete batch, runs grasp_3d_review (grasp-centre stages only; TCP-pose stages are not reviewed), and immediately executes in the SAME call when all checks pass with zero warnings/risks, the preview is planned (every move stage met its tolerances) and there are no downgrade_reasons (otherwise it returns the preview plan_id with downgrade_reasons, without moving). mode=preflight plans without moving the robot, caches plan_id for mode=execute, and returns numerical costs/tolerances/advisory_notes with 0 images. mode=direct explicitly previews and immediately executes without returning for model review. mode=reach takes the current observation_id and 1..16 move stages (id, kind, arm, position_m, quaternion_xyzw, or the grasp_centre_m pose fields, and optional tolerance fields only) and solves IK for each candidate pose independently from the joints measured at the call: no plan, no cache, no motion, and every stage is answered (no stop at the first unreachable pose); use it to compare candidate grasp/place poses before preview. It returns stage_count, reachable_stage_count and stage_results[id] with ok (joints within the limits meet the stage's effective tolerances), ik (position_error_m in m, orientation_error_rad in rad; when not ok the closest residuals and, if a position-first solve reached the position, position_priority with the quaternion reachable there), tolerances, reached (position_m, quaternion_xyzw, approach_axis) and, when ok, q_rad and joint_travel_rad (rad); a failure of the whole query (e.g. ik_service_unreachable) is a tool error naming its reason. Optional plan_update submits or updates task_plan inline in the same call without a separate task_plan round trip. stages run in list order on the one arm; IDs are unique. move uses position_m + quaternion_xyzw for a measured gripper_frame_link target in so101_base metres. To grasp or carry an object, move may instead give grasp_centre_m (where the object centre sits between the jaws, so101_base metres) + object_width_m (its extent along the jaw line, metres) with quaternion_xyzw or fixed_jaw_yaw_deg (degrees, straight-down approach); the gripper_frame_link target is computed from the gripper geometry and reported in stage_plans[<stage>].grasp_centre. Routes use successive move stages, not via fields. There are no joint/home/reset kinds; a return uses saved measured poses. Every move has its own arm speed and optional gripper_goal_normalized/speed; gripper_motion fractions synchronize that jaw within THIS move. Without fractions its jaw runs after measured arrival. A gripper stage requires goal_normalized (0 closed, 1 open), not gripper or goal. observe requires reason and pauses the arm at that checkpoint. Later stages remain cached. After inspecting RGB, execute the same plan_id to continue only if its current-state validity check passes; otherwise preview a new plan. Optional checkpoint_after_gripper=true (on a grasp/gripper stage or the batch) pauses after a jaw stage before the next move stage (pre-lift) to inspect finger contact and grip_facts in RGB before continuing the cached plan_id; or use min_aperture_m/max_aperture_m [0..0.1372m] to conditionally pause only when measured_aperture_m falls outside the expected bounds (valid grasps continue into lift without pausing). Use tolerance_preset (tight, normal, relaxed, coarse, unconstrained_orientation) or position_tolerance_m/orientation_tolerance_rad per stage, and set stall_guard_preset="contact_stop" specifically on contact descent/press stages (keep batch default "off" for free-space transits). Arrival/closed-jaw commands do not prove contact, support or retention. mode=inspect accepts plan_id for cached evidence, action_id for executed measured/planned paths, or trajectory_ref for an existing artifact; path_kind selects measured/planned. Auxiliary review is reserved; the main model owns execution approval. Usage: preview/preflight/execute_if_clean/direct require current observation_id and either 1..32 stages, source_plan_id + start_from_stage_id (with optional stage_overrides to recompile remaining stages from current measured state), or plan_id + skip_failed_stage/partial stages (from repair_action); execute accepts plan_id, optional action_id, optional image_delivery and expected_cursor/expected_revision; inspect requires exactly one plan_id/action_id/trajectory_ref plus inspection options. Example checkpoint preview: {"observation_id":"obs1","stages":[{"id":"check","kind":"observe","reason":"inspect current support"}]}. After reviewing a returned plan: {"mode":"execute","plan_id":"p1","expected_cursor":0,"expected_revision":0}. Explicit continuation after a paused/failed stage: {"mode":"preview","observation_id":"obs2","source_plan_id":"p1","start_from_stage_id":"carry","stage_overrides":{"carry":{"position_tolerance_m":0.015}}} or {"mode":"preview","observation_id":"obs2","plan_id":"p1","skip_failed_stage":true}. Not available on this robot, so absent from this schema: grasp-angle pose input (top-down angle triples), named grip-guard presets (they need the measured empty-close reading of this gripper), joint-travel admission limits, obstacle-crossing clearance arcs, obstacle and held-object geometry review, and converting object-table rows into obstacle boxes. Gripper stage syntax: {"id":"open","kind":"gripper","arm":"right","goal_normalized":1}; choose the goal from the intended action.

tool_definitions.name: robot_action_status
tool_definitions.description: Read a saved action request and execution receipt without executing it again. summary keeps execution/partial/failure evidence and a full-result lookup; full reads original stored evidence. Inspect receipt.status and result_observation_id; tool dispatch success does not establish physical or task success. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"action_id":"act_1","detail":"full"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_capabilities
tool_definitions.description: Read coordinate/TCP conventions, supported action modes, native limits, speed/gripper semantics and current budget without moving. Startup supplies capabilities; later summary reads may report unchanged static values. full repeats the complete capability record. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"detail":"full"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_contact_overlay
tool_definitions.description: Draw the measured gripper_frame_link, the fixed and moving fingertips at the measured jaw angle and their midpoint, plus caller-requested midpoint targets, on saved calibrated RGB. Returns labeled robot-geometry metadata and an overlay image; measured and requested positions remain distinct. Uses original-image coordinates and no robot motion. Image overlap does not establish object contact or clearance. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"arms":["right"],"camera_id":"fixed","observation_id":"obs_1"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_information
tool_definitions.description: Read static robot knowledge or the latest published calibration without motion. default returns briefing, original URDF, supplemental physical parameters and native geometry reference; named sections return their detailed records. calibration does not capture a new frame. resources lists file IDs; resource returns an actor-readable file reference for client.artifact. geometry_image returns an illustrative image, not a measured scene. Unknown robots/resources return unavailable. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"section":"resources"} ; {"resource_id":"geometry_model","section":"resource"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_observe
tool_definitions.description: Capture current permitted RGB, same-frame measured joint/EE/gripper state and budgets. Returns observation_id, state/calibration metadata and images. Optional image_delivery selects 'none' (0 images; fast numeric state refresh), 'focus_roi' (1:1 native-sensor local crops around focus_3d), 'head_only' (fixed RGB only) or 'all' (all calibrated views). Optional focus_3d projects a 3D sphere (target_m in so101_base m and/or detected 3D object_id such as 'o2', radius_m in m) through calibrated K and measured T_world_camera (including live wrist FK) to 1:1 native-resolution crops without capturing a new frame or replacing the current observation_id, returning crop_xywh_px=[crop_x,crop_y,w,h], projected_center_uv_px and full_uv = [crop_x + local_u, crop_y + local_v] for geometry_query. Optional camera_id with manual roi/scale inspects a zoomed single-view crop on demand (mutually exclusive with focus_3d). No hidden object/score access. summary avoids repeating unchanged calibration; full repeats it. Fixed-camera observations here and in robot_action / robot_wait replies also carry the frame's VGGT-estimated object table (ids o1..oN: centre, top/bottom z, footprint, tilt, support, quality) plus a point-cloud artifact handle for scene3d_helpers; robot_observe adds an id overlay image. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {} ; {"image_delivery":"none"} ; {"focus_3d":{"patch_px":256,"radius_m":0.06,"target_m":[0.22,0.0,0.06]}} ; {"focus_3d":{"object_id":"o2"},"image_delivery":"focus_roi"}

tool_definitions.name: robot_policy_step
tool_definitions.description: Delegate one local intent to the matched ARX X5 pi0.5 policy when enabled. Uses current three-camera RGB/proprioception, executes only the selected prefix and returns an action receipt plus fresh feedback. Default prefix=5 is 0.20 simulated seconds at 25 Hz; each row costs a native step and native success stops execution. The actor still selects targets and the next goal; prompt text naming an arm or distance is not a movement constraint. Requires the initial task plan. Review feedback before another prefix; do not delegate an entire task. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"observation_id":"obs_1","prefix":5,"prompt":"Adjust the local grasp, then return feedback."}

examples.prompt: Adjust the local grasp, then return feedback.

tool_definitions.name: robot_wait
tool_definitions.description: Hold the arm at its last commanded joint goals and retain the gripper command for 1..50 control steps of 0.05 s each (20 Hz, real time); the world keeps moving during the wait and while you reason. Returns execution receipt, chronological camera samples, final RGB/state and whether that observation remains current. Use for external motion or settling. Requires the initial task plan; no automatic phase detection or retry. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"native_steps":10,"observation_id":"obs_1"}

tool_definitions.name: robotic_view
tool_definitions.description: Calculate a wrist-camera look-at pose from your chosen eye position, target point and image-up direction, using the current formal camera-to-link6 calibration. Optical axes are right/down/forward. Returns a link6 position and quaternion_xyzw inside suggested robot_action preview arguments; this tool does not call preview or execute. Review a separate robot_action preview before choosing to move. Prefer an otherwise free wrist for a useful complementary view; do not disturb a holding arm merely for a picture. Choose eye/target coordinates from permitted evidence, optionally using existing geometry_query; this tool does not infer target depth or select a viewpoint. No new image, model call, IK, obstacle avoidance, visibility, contact, retention or task-success check is performed. A calculated pose is not proof of a safe or useful view. Camera motion uses the existing action path and consumes its normal budget if you execute it. The suggested preview is grounded in this observation and may become stale after another action.

observation_id.description: Current idle formal observation ID, 1–200 characters; historical or in-motion observations are rejected.

camera_id.description: Existing calibrated wrist camera ID, 1–100 characters, rigidly attached to native link6 through a disclosed fixed-joint chain. Fixed head cameras are unsupported.

eye_position_m.description: Exactly three finite numbers [x,y,z]: caller-selected desired camera optical center in metres in the observation calibration reference frame (native env_origin). This is not the link6 position.

target_position_m.description: Exactly three finite numbers [x,y,z]: caller-estimated or hypothesized look-at point in the SAME reference frame/metres. Must differ from eye_position_m by at least 1e-6 m. No object location is inferred.

up_vector.description: Exactly three finite numbers: nonzero desired image-up direction in the SAME reference frame; magnitude is ignored. Its angle to the view axis must have sine greater than 1e-6. Choose explicitly; no default or automatic roll is selected.

tool_definitions.name: run_begin
tool_definitions.description: Start a NI-RUA task, or re-read its briefing. Call this first, before any other NI-RUA tool, and again whenever your earlier context may have been lost (after a context compaction, in a new session, or after a resume). It has no physical effect: it does not move the robot and captures no observation. No inputs.

tool_definitions.name: run_finish
tool_definitions.description: Declare that you have finished the current NI-RUA task, or that you cannot continue it. It has no physical effect: it does not move the robot, release torque, end the environment or judge task success. It closes the open turn as completed and records summary as the turn's final answer for the operator and replay; afterwards the other NI-RUA tools are refused (external_turn_closed) until run_begin opens the next turn. Called while no turn is open, it records the summary in a turn of its own and closes it. It does not stop helper programs that are still running (program_run jobs): read program_status first; a job paused for your review stops with program_run resume decision=reject, any other job runs until its work time ends or the operator stops the run.

summary.description: Final statement, 1 to 16000 characters, required, no default: what was done, the evidence for the outcome, and what is uncertain or why you stopped.

tool_definitions.name: stereo_guide
tool_definitions.description: Mark your source pixel and draw its epipolar constraint on a second current formal RGB image. Images are returned in source-then-target order, at original dimensions; cyan marks the source point and a thin cyan line marks the target constraint. Originals are preserved. target_line=[a,b,c] means a*u+b*v+c=0 in rectified target pixels, with sqrt(a*a+b*b)=1; target_endpoints are its intersections with the pixel-center rectangle [0,width-1] x [0,height-1]. Calibrated pinhole and OpenCV radial-tangential (opencv / opencv_plumb_bob) cameras are supported. Same camera, baseline below 1e-6 m, degenerate epipolar direction, or no nonzero line segment inside the target image is rejected. The entire line is a geometric constraint, not an identified match or a positive-depth interval. Select and verify the SAME physical feature yourself using image appearance and other permitted evidence, then use existing geometry_query triangulate if appropriate. A small line distance or reprojection error alone cannot validate semantic correspondence. Source-pixel and calibration errors affect the constraint. Occlusion, feature visibility, depth, object pose, collision and task success remain untested. This tool does not match points, triangulate, call a model, acquire a new observation or execute any action.

observation_id.description: Current idle formal observation ID, 1–200 characters. Both cameras must belong to this same observation; stale or in-motion observations are rejected.

source_camera_id.description: Source calibrated camera ID, 1–100 characters. Its original actor RGB supplies the pixel you chose.

target_camera_id.description: Different target calibrated camera ID, 1–100 characters, in the same reference frame and observation. Its original RGB receives the epipolar line.

source_pixel.description: Exactly two finite numbers [u,v], in original source-image pixels (u right, v down), with 0 <= u < width and 0 <= v < height. No resized/cropped display coordinates. Choose the same distinctive physical feature you intend to find in the target image; source localization error propagates to the line.

tool_definitions.name: task_plan
tool_definitions.description: Save or read this episode's brief ordinary-language task plan, dynamic attention list and short evidence ledger. Submit plan before the first physical action, including a wait, and always include ledger explicitly (use [] when no material prerequisite is unresolved). Suggested plan headings: Task understanding; Approach + completion. Keep only currently relevant concerns, evidence/adjustments and check times in attention. When a material task-result prerequisite is unresolved and a later decision depends on it, keep only one to three short ledger rows. The ledger has at most 3 task prerequisites or expected events with status=pending|supported|contradicted|unknown, a short permitted evidence basis and the next distinguishing check. After contradicted evidence, change the contact, route or target mechanism, or state that no distinguishing next step is supported. It is an advisory decision boundary: completed motion, preview success and closed gripper do not prove an object result, and pending rows do not block useful actions. Add, replace or remove rows as evidence changes, without updating after every motion. Prefer normal task-progress actions' final observations; add a probe only when missing evidence affects the next decision. Plans, attention and ledger are advisory and do not execute or constrain later actions. update accepts plan, attention, ledger or any combination; omitted fields are retained and [] clears a list; when a ledger value changes, include the replacement ledger. Repeating the same field values at the same observation returns status=unchanged without a new revision; the same values at a newer observation record a new judgment source. submit/update return a plan ID and acknowledgement; read returns the current plan, attention, ledger and field-source observation IDs, and accepts only operation. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"ledger":[],"observation_id":"obs_1","operation":"submit","plan":"Task understanding: move the visible target to its support. Approach + completion: choose a clear grasp and route, release, then verify stable placement."} ; {"attention":[{"check":"Use visible object-to-finger alignment; if it shifted, adjust the placement approach.","concern":"The object may have shifted in the gripper.","when":"From the normal transfer action's final observation, before placement."}],"operation":"update"} ; {"attention":[],"operation":"update"} ; {"operation":"read"}

examples.plan: Task understanding: move the visible target to its support. Approach + completion: choose a clear grasp and route, release, then verify stable placement.

attention.concern: The object may have shifted in the gripper.
attention.check: Use visible object-to-finger alignment; if it shifted, adjust the placement approach.
attention.when: From the normal transfer action's final observation, before placement.

tool_definitions.name: vision_compare
tool_definitions.description: Track a caller-selected textured patch between saved RGB frames without a new capture, action or model request. Returns texture-correspondence status, pixel displacement and match quality; optional reference tracking gives target-minus-reference displacement. Select target texture in BEFORE original-image pixels, excluding fingers/background. lost/ambiguous means insufficient correspondence, not a dropped object. Correspondence does not prove semantic identity, grasp, contact, metric motion or task success; use optional vision_review when available for uncertain visual interpretation. Do not repeat an unchanged frame pair and ROI. Examples (replace IDs/pixels with actual saved evidence): {"after_observation_id":"obs_2","before_observation_id":"obs_1","camera_id":"fixed","roi":[100,100,40,40]}

tool_definitions.name: vision_review
tool_definitions.description: Request an optional helper-model assessment using saved permitted RGB. evidence_mode=images (default) judges the described target's retention/release from a before/after pair; operation also checks ordered action receipts and measured state for a named manipulation phase/expected_result.
